pr_title: Process persistent worker env before spawning
pr_body:
Previously for iOS builds with persistent workers some required
environment variables like SDKROOT and DEVELOPER_DIR were not passed to
persistent workers when they were spawned. Now we include the
environment variables from the `LocalEnvProvider` that would be used for
fallback builds.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223
pr_comments:
See more context about this on https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223

I'm not sure if this is the right solution for all workers or not, but I submitted it to start the discussion.

It looks like an alternative solution here would be to move the logic from https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/645a35e1ce0f9f0025e9120399f2e7b77b4841b8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/apple/XcodeLocalEnvProvider.java#L104

to AppleConfiguration https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/645a35e1ce0f9f0025e9120399f2e7b77b4841b8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/apple/AppleConfiguration.java#L130-L134

I'm not sure what other implications that would have

I don't know enough about how workers work, so I'll just have to ask a question that hopefully @philwo can answer.

`DEVELOPER_DIR` is controlled based on the version of Xcode currently selected (passing `--xcode_version` to Bazel) and based on wherever the `xcode-locator` tool detects those Xcode installations to be, and `SDKROOT` is controlled IIRC by the `--apple_platform_type` flag, which can be past manually but is typically used via a configuration transition from `ios_application`, `watchos_application`, etc.

If we have a persistent worker that spans multiple compilation actions, are we guaranteed that actions with different `(--xcode_version, --apple_platform_type)` pairs will be sent to workers that have been launched with the correct environments? We don't want a situation where a worker is launched with an `iPhoneSimulator` SDK root but it gets sent compilation actions for watchOS libraries, for example.

We likely already have this problem. If you see in my original post here https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6223 the variables that are currently passed, they contain both the SDK and the Xcode version already. I'm not sure if those are ready anywhere by Bazel or Xcode's toolchain but if they are the persistent workers would already be specific to these.


--
Keith Smiley

Yes, this is guaranteed. The environment with which a worker was launched
is part of its WorkerKey. If you have two workers of the same kind but
different environments, Bazel will launch independent instances and route
to them correctly.

issue_context.title: Some environment variables not passed to persistent workers
issue_context.body:
I'm working on creating a persistent worker to support incremental compilation [for Swift](https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_swift/issues/48). In doing so, the first issue I hit, was the lack of required environment variables being passed to the newly created persistent workers.

When running the builds normally, this is the environment passed to the build:

```
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
TMPDIR=/var/folders/5b/bs2_gmk512147rfb9c6278f80000gp/T/
SDKROOT=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/iPhoneSimulator.platform/Developer/SDKs/iPhoneSimulator12.0.sdk
XCODE_VERSION_OVERRIDE=10.0.0
__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING=0x1F6:0x0:0x0
PWD=/private/var/tmp/_bazel_...
SHLVL=1
APPLE_SDK_PLATFORM=iPhoneSimulator
APPLE_SDK_VERSION_OVERRIDE=12.0
```

But the persistent workers are launched with this environment:

```
XCODE_VERSION_OVERRIDE=10.0.0
PWD=/private/var/tmp/_bazel_...
SHLVL=1
APPLE_SDK_PLATFORM=iPhoneSimulator
APPLE_SDK_VERSION_OVERRIDE=12.0
```

This results in the underlying [script](https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_swift/blob/c8138ccf8cd798aefc9533840fcab72546e4c46c/tools/wrappers/xcrunwrapper.sh#L38) to fail since `SDKROOT` is required but not defined.

Is this variable intentionally excluded from persistent workers? Or is there a place we need to whitelist this variable to be passed along? I am testing with bazel 0.17.1
comments: `DEVELOPER_DIR` is also missing from the persistent worker env here

Ok I think I discovered why this is the case. When building locally we hit this codepath: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/18bd7dec9609ff8924d9ebed5f14be523df4eec0/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/sandbox/DarwinSandboxedSpawnRunner.java#L224-L225 which adds the variables we want from here https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/1f684e1b87cd8881a0a4b33e86ba66743e32d674/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/apple/XcodeLocalEnvProvider.java#L66-L108 but persistent workers don't call this local env rewrite logic https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/5a1ed1f24e74f8a608ee145133f399c1f34a8390/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/worker/WorkerSpawnRunner.java#L131 meaning they don't add the variables we were hoping for.

I'm not really sure what an acceptable solution for this is since I don't think normally we'd want to pass persistent workers the local environment logic, but in this case it's required for quite a few arguments.
@allevato assuming you have some context on these, any thoughts?

I've run into the same problem in my worker prototype, and my solution was to hack it by having my wrapper set DEVELOPER_DIR and SDKROOT by querying xcode-select/xcrun manually if they're not already set. Not ideal.
Sounds like a problem with persistent workers. @keith wanna send us a patch? :-) cc: @philwo
@buchgr I'm happy to submit that fix, but is that a reasonable one? Just based on the naming tying the local environment objects to the persistent workers sounds like they're intentionally attached
I've submitted a PR that fixes it in this way, please let me know what you think! https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/6287

review_comments: I've seen some different things passed for `/tmp` here, I assume there's something other than this to be more platform agnostic that I should pass?
